Subject: Private deployment validation - FluxGrid x Redwood

Hi Jordan + Evelyn,

Thanks again for the quick intro earlier this week. FluxGrid is preparing a private deployment of Redwood Inference (customer-managed VPC) to support our on-prem latency SLAs for the EdgeFleet product. Before committing to a Dedicated contract we want a technical validation run with a small proof-of-concept (model + sample traffic) to ensure compatibility with our networking/KMS constraints and to get a smoke test plan we can run in our staging lab.

High level:
- Target model: open-llama-13B (we'll likely serve a 4-bit quantized variant)
- Peak concurrency: 30 req/s with 128-token avg responses
- Data controls: all inference requests must stay in our VPC; no persistent copy in Redwood control plane
- Key concerns: KMS integration, egress rules, KV cache behavior for short contexts

Attached are our initial solution blueprint and a short checklist. Can Redwood validate the reference design and propose an in-lab test window next week?

Attachments: fluxgrid_solution_blueprint.pdf, fluxgrid_smoke_test_checklist.xlsx

Best,

Thanks — added a few notes after an initial pass on the FluxGrid blueprint (attached as rwinference_private_reference_notes.pdf). High-level comments and validation items:

1) Sizing and instance class
- For a quantized 13B model serving ~30req/s with 128-token responses, recommend 4x A10G-equivalent GPUs in a pinned pool for predictable latency. We can also test N:M packing with 2x higher batch sizes to assess efficiency gains.

2) Model packaging
- Provide both the float32 and 4-bit quantized artifacts. Redwood runtime will prefer the quantized artifact for cost/speed but we need a float fallback for correctness checks. Please include tokenizer version and any custom prompt templates.

3) KV cache & context
- Short context (<512 tokens) should benefit from local KV caching; however, if you expect high context churn, we should test cache hit rates. We'll instrument per-token cache hit/miss metrics.

4) Networking / VPC
- Two viable options: (A) VPC peering with Redwood control plane + strict egress rules; (B) Air-gapped with API proxy inside your VPC (we'll send a lightweight agent image). Option A is faster to onboard; Option B gives maximum control. Need to confirm whether your security team allows peering to a Redwood-managed control plane endpoint.

5) KMS / keys
- We support both customer-managed keys (bring-your-own KMS) and a proxied KMS flow. For HSM-backed keys we'll need to validate the crypto handshake in the staging window.

6) Observability & logs
- We'll enable token-level latency traces and per-request metadata but will not persist prompt content unless you opt-in. Confirm retention window (default 30d).

Smoke test plan (short):
- Connectivity: validate VPC routes, KMS handshake, and agent startup (10m)
- Baseline: serve sample traffic at 5 req/s for 10m, verify correctness vs float fallback
- Load: ramp to 30 req/s sustained for 15m, record P95 latency, error rate <1%
- Edge cases: network partition simulation for 2m to validate failover to fallback model

I'll present these notes in the technical review. Attaching rwinference_private_reference_notes.pdf (internal summary).

—Evelyn

Quick note on security items we must confirm before the in-lab run:
- SOC2 attestation or equivalent for any Redwood-managed control-plane components in the path. If FluxGrid requires air-gapped, mark option B as preferred.
- Encryption: TLS1.2+ for in-transit; customer-managed KMS for at-rest keys. Clarify whether FluxGrid will require HSM-backed attestations.
- Audit logs: need to capture request-level metadata but we must exclude PII/PHI. Please confirm sample payloads for a dry-run.
- PenTest windows: if you plan to run penetration testing against the deployed stack, provide a schedule and scope 72 hours prior.

Maya — can you loop in your security lead (name + email) so we can coordinate the evidence exchange? Also confirm whether FluxGrid has any regional data residency constraints beyond US.

-Diego
